messages:
marta (design): quick heads-up 12  looking at density complaints in the rules editor tests. idea: reduce badge chrome and rely on bold labels + numeric priority to lower visual weight. keeps preview canvas clearer. thoughts?

leo (pm): I like lighter chrome but make sure priority remains scannable. users often scan for 1/2/3 not color. also want to revisit the primary action wording on the sim panel: 'Run simulation' vs 'Start simulation' 12 which is clearer?

nina (uxwriter): 'Run simulation' is better imo. it's task-oriented and matches analytics event names we already use. Keep verbs consistent: "Run" for actions, "Start" reserved for long-running infra tasks.

akash (frontend): Implementation-wise we can tone down badge borders and switch to semi-bold label + a small numeric chip. For keyboard focus, preserve a visible focus ring on badges when tabbed — don't remove outlines.

sylvie (a11y): Important: focus ring color must meet contrast and not rely on suppressed chrome. Also don't hide badge text when in compact mode; screen readers need text. Use `aria-label` like "Priority 1, High" if you shorten visual text to "1".

marta (design): good point. other nit: the preview simulation focus trap currently steals focus when a snapshot is taken. users can't keyboard-navigate back to the rules quickly. propose moving snapshot confirmation into a non-modal toast and leaving focus where it was.

akash (frontend): Agree. We'll change snapshot flow: toast with link "View snapshot" (opens drawer) and focus stays on the previously focused control. Also add `aria-live=polite` for the toast and `aria-atomic=true` for the summary text.

leo (pm): For conflict resolution UX: when two rules conflict, show a small inline pill: "Conflict with Rule X (ID hidden)" and an action "Open resolver". Keep pill subtle to avoid interrupting editing flow.

nina (uxwriter): Copy suggestion: "Conflicts with 'Allow beta users' — Resolve". Avoid exposing internal IDs; prefer friendly names. If name not available, say "an earlier rule" and link to highlight.

sylvie (a11y): Inline conflict pill should use `role=button` if clickable and have clear accessible name. If it shifts layout, avoid moving keyboard focus. Provide `aria-describedby` for the quick explanation.

marta (design): Another accessibility/visual tradeoff: compact mode hides drag handles to save space. Tests show discoverability drops. Proposal: in compact mode show a subtle always-visible micro-handle (6px wide) with tooltip on hover, but no heavy chrome.

akash (frontend): Micro-handle workable. We'll make hit target 32px but only show visual 6px strip so density preserved. Use `touch-action` long-press for reorder on mobile.

sylvie (a11y): Ensure micro-handle is reachable by keyboard and has `aria-label="Reorder rule"`. Provide alternative reorder controls (move up/down) accessible via a keyboard-only menu.

leo (pm): One more: validation messages during sim should be concise and actionable. Example: instead of "Rule X missing match condition: backend_field missing", say "Rule missing match condition — add a match to run this rule". Also offer "Auto-fix" only if safe.

nina (uxwriter): Agreed. Tone neutral, action-first. Examples: "Missing match condition. Add condition" / "Priority conflict. Resolve". Keep messages <80 chars where possible.

marta (design): Action items: Akash implement lighter badge + numeric chip + focus ring; Sylvie publish a11y checklist for focus, toast, and micro-handle; Nina finalize short strings; Leo to decide on snapshot flow confirmation language and flag gating. I'll update the mock (compact vs full) and push to the design review board.

design-bot: Prototype link: https://figma.redwood.design/proto/density-focus-rail 12 comments enabled.

akash (frontend): I'll start `feat/density-tweak` branch with keyboard tests for reorder and toast behavior.

sylvie (a11y): I'll add the checklist to the ticket and run a quick NVDA pass on the prototype tomorrow.

marta (design): thanks team 12 we'll circle in design sync and aim to ship behind a flag for initial user testing. :thumbsup:
